title: I know you'll come
goal: Report facts and beliefs with -DIğI and -(y)AcAğI as noun clauses.

intro.text: Turkish has no word for **that** in *I know that you came*. The clause becomes a noun: `-DIk` or `-(y)AcAk`, a possessive for the doer, then the case the main verb needs: *Geldiğini biliyorum* (I know you came), *Geleceğine sevindim* (I'm glad you'll come), *Haklı olduğundan eminim* (I'm sure she's right).

vocab.en: aware (of: genitive; bunun farkındayım: I'm aware of it)

exercises.question: *Ali'nin geleceğini biliyorum.* What do I know?

why.1: **That Ali came** would be *Ali'nin geldiğini*, with `-DIk`.
why.2: **Whether** would be *gelip gelmeyeceğini*, with the positive and the negative.

exercises.en: I heard that Selin had moved to Ankara.

reject.why: *Duydum* needs a noun as its object: `-DIk`, the possessive and the accusative, *taşındığını*.
The clause is the object of *duydum*, so it takes the accusative, after the n of the third person: *taşındığını*.

exercises.hint: `-DIk`, the possessive for **she**, then the case *duymak* needs.

exercises.label: *çalışmak* + *biliyor*: she knows that I studied, that you studied…
exercises.explain: `-DIk` becomes *-dığ-* before a vowel, then the possessive and the accusative: *çalış-tığ-ım-ı*. For **they**: *çalış-tık-ları-n-ı*. **You** and **he** look the same: *çalıştığını*.

exercises.prompt: I didn't know you were ill.

reject.why: *Olduğumu* is **that I was** ill. **You** were ill: *olduğunu*, or *olduğunuzu*.
*Bilmiyordum* needs a noun object: *hasta olduğunu*, with *olmak*, `-DIk` and the accusative.

exercises.explain: *hasta ol-duğ-un-u*: the adjective goes through *olmak*, then `-DIk`, your possessive and the accusative.

accept: I am sure that Ali will keep this secret.
I am sure Ali will keep [this|the] secret.
I am sure that Ali will keep the secret.
I am [certain|convinced] (that) Ali will keep [this|the] secret.

exercises.en: She proved that she was right.

exercises.prompt: Murat bu sırrı bilmediğini iddia ediyor.
exercises.text: Murat claims that he does not know this secret.
accept: Murat claims he does not know this secret.

exercises.question: *Haklı ___ eminim.* (I'm sure you're right.) Which form fits?

why.1: *Emin olmak* doesn't take the accusative: you are sure **of** something, so the ablative.
why.2: The dative goes with *inanmak* or *sevinmek*; *emin olmak* takes the ablative.

exercises.prompt: We were so glad you came.
exercises.explain: *Sevinmek* takes the dative: *gel-diğ-in-e*. *Gelmene* is also right: with feelings, both `-DIk` and `-mA` work.
Before the consonant of *-leri*, `-(y)AcAk` keeps its k; then the n of the third person and the accusative: *gel-ecek-leri-n-i*.

accept: I suspect that Ali is lying.
I suspect (that) Ali [was lying|lied|has lied|is telling a lie|told a lie|has been lying].

exercises.prompt: I noticed that the door was open.
accept: Ben kapının açık olduğunu fark ettim.

reject.why: A noun doer takes the genitive in a noun clause: *kapının açık olduğunu*.
*Fark etmek* takes the accusative: *olduğunu fark ettim*.

exercises.explain: *Kapı-nın açık ol-duğ-u-n-u fark ettim*: the doer in the genitive, the clause in the accusative.

accept: He is not aware that he made a mistake.
He is not aware [he made|that he has made|he has made] a mistake.
She is not aware (that) she [made|has made] a mistake.
[He|She] [is unaware|does not realize|does not realise] (that) [he|she] [made|has made] a mistake.
